# Rosalind Penrose

## Overview

- **Age:** 45 years old (at intro)  <sub>[v2 c21 P34](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0034), [v2 c21 P54](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0054), [v2 c23 P10](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0010)</sub>
- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v2 c21 P28](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0028), [v2 c21 P45](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0045)</sub>
- **Status:** Alive  <sub>[v4 c3 P30](../source/v04-c03.md#nw-v04-c03-p0030)</sub>
- **Origin:** East Welby  <sub>[v2 c21 P86](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0086)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Mother Rosalind  <sub>[v3 c23 P4](../source/v03-c23.md#nw-v03-c23-p0004)</sub>

## Appearance

Rosalind is a tiny woman with thick, wavy, snow-white hair that she thoughtfully styles in flattering puffs and coils. Below her hair, she has a youthful, rosy-cheeked face featuring sweet lips, dimples, and large, gentle wood-brown eyes with flecks of gold. She favors delicate, youthful dresses adorned with frills, lace, or floral patterns, such as delicate cream muslin with light roses, vibrant deep red dresses, or forget-me-not organdy.

_Sources: [v2 c21 P45](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0045), [v2 c22 P2](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0002), [v2 c23 P5](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0005), [v2 c27 P22](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0022), [v2 c28 P57](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0057)_

## Personality

Rosalind is a romantic, imaginative, and youthful soul who deeply enjoys imaginative play, pretending, and hosting small tea gatherings. Although peculiar and prone to defying social norms—such as disregarding strict dietary rules and ignoring standard expectations for women her age—she possesses an exceptionally kind, warm, and hospitable nature. Underneath her daydreaming and romantic heart lies a capable and practical side when occasion requires. She detests the thought of aging and initially withdrew into a solitary existence, though she deeply treasures young people and kindred spirits.

_Sources: [v2 c21 P54](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0054), [v2 c21 P58](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0058), [v2 c21 P62](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0062), [v2 c22 P6](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0006), [v2 c22 P7](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0007), [v2 c23 P9](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0009), [v2 c23 P29](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0029), [v2 c27 P29](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0029)_

## History

Rosalind lived for years in isolation at Echo Cottage in Welby alongside her live-in handmaiden Belinda the Fourth, having withdrawn from social life after her youth engagement broke down. One autumn afternoon, Nell Harcourt and Isolde Pembroke stumbled upon her stone dwelling, beginning a close friendship between Nell and Rosalind as kindred spirits. Later that winter, Nell introduced Cedric Stanhope to Rosalind, initiating a warm bond between her and her former fiancé's young son. After learning from Cedric's letter that Rosalind remained unmarried, Stephen Stanhope returned from Boston and reconnected with her at Echo Cottage. The two rekindled their relationship and married in late August beneath her garden's honeysuckle trellis. Following their wedding, Rosalind relocated to Boston with Stephen, Cedric, and Belinda, returning each summer to inhabit Echo Cottage.

_Sources: [v2 c21 P28](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0028), [v2 c21 P62](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0062), [v2 c22 P7](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0007), [v2 c23 P3](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0003), [v2 c23 P26](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0026), [v2 c28 P35](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0035), [v2 c28 P70](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0070), [v2 c29 P5](../source/v02-c29.md#nw-v02-c29-p0005), [v2 c29 P10](../source/v02-c29.md#nw-v02-c29-p0010), [v2 c30 P29](../source/v02-c30.md#nw-v02-c30-p0029), [v2 c30 P30](../source/v02-c30.md#nw-v02-c30-p0030), [v2 c30 P33](../source/v02-c30.md#nw-v02-c30-p0033), [v3 c23 P1](../source/v03-c23.md#nw-v03-c23-p0001), [v3 c23 P2](../source/v03-c23.md#nw-v03-c23-p0002), [v4 c3 P30](../source/v04-c03.md#nw-v04-c03-p0030)_

## Background by volume

- Named Rosalind by her father because he adored the fragrance of lavender sheets that kept him awake when he met her mother in East Welby  <sub>[v2 c21 P86](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0086)</sub>
- Engaged in her youth to Stephen Stanhope 25 years prior, but they separated following a disagreement  <sub>[v2 c21 P36](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0036), [v2 c22 P9](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0009)</sub>
- Lived in the old stone Echo Cottage built by her father eight decades past  <sub>[v2 c21 P28](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0028), [v2 c22 P7](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0007)</sub>
- Employed young girls from the Bowman family sequentially as live-in handmaidens, calling each of them 'Belinda' for convenience  <sub>[v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076)</sub>

## Quotes

> Pretending to be a girl myself comes so naturally when I am in their company. I really despise accepting that I am advanced in years.  <sub>[v2 c21 P62](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0062)</sub>

> A few women are old maids from birth, others attain the status of an old maid, and still others find old maidenhood forced on them.  <sub>[v2 c23 P13](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0013)</sub>

> I always prefer to execute things as thoroughly as I can, and because it was my fate to become an old maid, I resolved that I would be an exceptionally pleasant one.  <sub>[v2 c23 P15](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0015)</sub>

> Oh, at times, it seems to me that making friends serves no purpose. After a bit, they merely depart from your life, leaving behind an ache that exceeds the void existing before their arrival.  <sub>[v2 c27 P32](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0032)</sub>
